Subject: Demo failure: token/encoding mismatch seen with sdk-java-1.8

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. During the live run we started seeing generation truncation and garbled characters midway through longer responses. It only showed up when we used the sdk-java v1.8 client with our existing tokenization layer — v1.7 behaved fine.

What we observed:
- After ~700 tokens the stream stops emitting and we see a short set of replacement characters (e.g., �) then the response ends.
- Using the HTTP API directly (no SDK) the same prompt returns full output.
- We attached a small repro prompt (repro-prompt.txt) and compressed logs (sdk-logs-20261205.tar.gz). The logs include the client-side stream chunks and the server-side trace ids.

This is blocking our internal demo on Monday. Can you escalate and let us know if we should roll back to v1.7 on our end? We can be available for a quick debug session.

Thanks,
Olivia

On Sat, Dec 5, 2026 at 10:04 AM Vivek Kulkarni wrote:
> Folks — looping you in. Canopy hit a reproducible failure during a live demo when using sdk-java v1.8; direct HTTP calls are fine. Attached logs show stream chunk boundaries where replacement chars appear.

Thanks for the details and the repro, Vivek + Olivia. Initial triage notes below after quick look at logs and repro prompt.

What I see:
- The server sends full token stream (verified by trace ids in the server trace). The SDK client appears to be assembling stream frames into a single UTF-8 string, but at certain byte boundaries the client-side decoder drops a leading continuation byte and emits U+FFFD (replacement char) then closes the stream.
- This behavior correlates with the new framing/keepalive handling introduced in sdk-java v1.8 (PR#2451) which changed how partial UTF-8 sequences are buffered across websocket/http2 frames.
- There is also a suspicious KV-cache offset mismatch in the logs (offset jumps late in the stream) but I can't confirm whether that is a downstream symptom or unrelated.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Reproduce locally on a node with sdk-java v1.8 and the provided repro prompt. I will try to write a focused unit test that simulates partial multi-byte UTF-8 splits across frames.
2) If reproduced, prepare a 1.8.1 patch that restores the previous buffering semantics for UTF-8 continuation bytes; this should be low-risk.
3) If a patch is not ready before Monday demo, authorize a customer-scoped rollback of the client package to v1.7 for Canopy's bundles and optionally offer a short-lived feature flag at the server routing layer to force non-streaming (polled) responses as a fallback.

I'll start step (1) now and update the ticket: INF-789.

Karthik
